recipes.name: Chicken Chimichangas with Sour Cream Sauce
ingredients_raw: 2 large skinless, boneless chicken breast halves
1 (7 ounce) can chopped green chilies, divided

steps.text: Place the chicken breasts into a large saucepan. Pour in the water, and season with chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon salt, cumin, 1/4 teaspoon black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne pepper. Bring to a simmer over high heat, then reduce heat to medium-low, and simmer 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, stir in 4 ounces of green chiles, onion, and garlic; continue simmering until the liquid has reduced to 1 cup. Reserve remaining 3 ounces of chopped green chilies.
Remove the chicken, shred with two forks, and return to the onion mixture.

Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Whisk in the water and bouillon cube until the water has thickened and the bouillon cube has dissolved, about 4 minutes. Whisk in reserved 3 ounces of green chilies and the sour cream; season to taste with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Heat oil in a deep-fryer or large saucepan to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).

Place a tortilla onto your work surface, then spoon about 1/3 cup of the chicken filling halfway between the bottom edge and the center of the tortilla. Flatten the filling into rectangle shape with the back of a spoon. Sprinkle about 1 ounce of the Monterey Jack cheese over the filling.

Fold the bottom of the tortilla snugly over the filling, then fold in the left and right edges. Roll the chimichanga up to the top edge, forming a tight cylinder; secure the ends with wooden toothpicks. Repeat with the remaining ingredients.
Cook the chimichangas, 2 at a time, in the hot oil until they are crisp and golden brown on both sides, about 1 minute per side.
Drain on a paper towel-lined plate, and remove toothpicks.
Top with sour cream sauce to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Chimichangas with Sour Cream Sauce
raw_recipe.description: Green chiles and Monterey Jack cheese make these chimichangas special.

review.reviewBody: AMAZING! Followed the recipe to the tee with the exception of baking at 425 degrees for 15 minutes vs. deep frying.

This turned out really well; it's probably my favorite recipe from this site so far. I cooked mine in the air fryer instead of deep frying, but they still came out beautiful. The level of spiciness is just right, and the cream sauce was delightful. The recipe does take a while, but you can make the chicken ahead of time. I also think you could make it with canned chicken.

These were really good! I did increase the spice amounts, 1/2 tsp garlic powder and onion powder, 3/4 tsp salt. I also cut the chicken breasts in half and used 2 cups of water instead of 3. Added the onion and garlic in the beginning. Cook covered for 15 min and 30 min uncovered. Was able to breack apart the chicken with a wooden spoon.

OMG!! Better than restaurant taste! I used the instant pot to cook the chicken and reduce the sauce using the sautee function. Since i didn't have canned chili peppers, I used a few tablespoons of picante salsa. Also, I subbed homemade Greek yogurt for sourcream and homemade butterkäse for Monterey Jack, as I ran out of the latter. I fried the chimichangas for about 1.5 minutes in my fryer at 375. Perfect! I'm sure the recipe is great when followed to a Tee, but you have to improvise here and there when you don't have all the ingredients. Thanks for the recipe and video.

It was awesome! I doubled up on the seasoning like one other reviewer said to do as well. I didn’t use salt and pepper because I used Season All and Mrs. Dash instead. I made mine with skinless chicken thighs instead of breast meat and used the water that was suggested. Once I knew my chicken was done I used the excess water/broth for my sour cream sauce instead of the water and bouillon cube. I also used a little Tabasco sauce in my sour cream sauce to give it a bit more kick like one of the other reviews said. I baked mine and when baking I flipped mine halfway through as I wanted the color to brown evenly and be crunchy (the side that is face down browns the fastest). Once done, I brushed it one last time but with a cilantro lime butter. ????

Amazing recipe!! I read many of the reviews...thank you for submitting...then doubled the seasonings, rubbed in olive oil and baked at 425 degrees for about 22 mins. I also added a little more sour cream to the sauce and lots of salt and pepper. The sauce is a MUST!! It took about 3 hours from start to finish but it was well worth the time. This recipe is a KEEPER!!

I used bone in chicken thighs then boned after cooking. Homemade salsa on white rice. Vegetable medley sautéed in some chicken grease from main recipe. Doubled recipe portions. Brushed oil on tortilla and backed at 400 degrees for 12 minutes. Really good! Will be part of my rotation.

It was good, I didn’t fry them I baked them at 425F for 15 min after brushing them with some lime infused olive oil. I also think i will try doubling the spices next time as it had a very subtle flavour.

We loved this recipe, I have had Chimichangas but never thought to make them, but they are really pretty easy with these easy to follow steps. I made my chicken mixture the day before and just refrigerated it and did the sauce and final assembly the next day. I too adjusted the chicken seasoning just because we like a stronger flavoring. I also fried them, we hardly ever eat fried foods so it was a safe "go" for us, when you get the temperature just right (375) the oil really doesn't penetrate the tortilla and the chicken mixture was just like steamed. I also used one of my enameled steel pots for the even heat it provides. This was a delicious recipe and we will have it again, just not too often!

These are fantastic! I agree with the other reviews that 3 cups of water is too much. I used 2 cups and it was still a lot. Will try 1 cup next time. I mistakenly bought jalapeños instead of chilis. The were not very spicy and the flavor was amazing. Many layers. I misted the chimichangas wit a bit of oil and air fried them at 400 for 10 minutes flipping once.
Very tasty! I used my instant pot to cook the chicken since it was frozen, 12 minutes on high. I also baked the chimis at 425 for 15 minutes instead of frying. Turned out great, will make again!
My adult kids went crazy for these so they’ll be on the rotation for sure. I do recommend however, that you deep fry these in oil. It seals them and really gives them authentic flavor and crunch.

This was awesome! I doubled the recipe and froze some uncooked. I also used no fat Greek yogurt as a substitute for the sour cream! (Can’t tell the difference!) I also brushed with a little olive oil and air fried at 360 degrees for about 4 minutes on each side. I would make a head for a crowd. It was better that the local restaurant and juicy. I also did not measure the cheese inside. Sooooo Good!

This is pretty good but it is NOT quick and easy. 😂 First when I noted the cook time of the chicken, plus the fact that you need to cook down the “seasoned” water to 1c left of liquid - I knew I needed to use boneless chicken thighs to avoid dried out chicken and budget for this process to take closer to 30-40 min. Both good observations. The sour cream sauce - while good - needs some more seasoning - perhaps cumin, hot sauce and/or maybe even a little cheese? I added some chopped green onions but while it was tasty, is was borderline dull. Make sure you have a sense of humor when it comes time to assemble these; they’re a little frustrating and I ended up flipping the toothpicks around so I could start frying mine seam-side down. All in all - these were good for homemade chimichangas! We enjoyed! Served over a bed of lettuce and a side of Spanish Rice. Thanks SSTRAWDER!
With all the ratings saying how great it was I think I expected it to be so good but it wasn't. It just didnt have any flavor and the suace was also very bland. Not sure what all the hype was about.

As everyone else says, it's an amazing recipe. I have never made chimichangas before, so it was fun. It's a bit time consuming, so I wouldn't make this on a busy work night, but on a relaxing weekend, it was perfect. I noticed that the juice that was with the chicken wasn't thickening to 1cup after the allotted time, so I ended up pulling the chicken out to rest, and bumping up the temp on the sauce. I let it boil, stirring periodically, until it thickened. I then added the chicken back to it and continued with the recipe. The one change I made was to bake instead of deep frying. I brushed each with olive oil and baked at 425F for approximately 5 min and then flipped for another 5 min. I watched until they were the perfect golden brown. The creamy sauce was delicious. It tasted like jalapeno poppers. It was a complimentary flavor to the chicken...and I could use this on other dishes as well. I paired it with pinto beans and guacamole. Overall, this was a fun and easy recipe. I look forward to making it again.

Since two people have problems with chilies, I substituted them with some green pepper and green onions, onions as a garnish. We love sauces so I doubled the recipe, put it in a serving bowl where people could take as much or as little as they wanted. Absolutely Delicious!!!!

Found this awesome online Chicken Chimichanga recipe that's a game-changer. Super easy steps, no fancy ingredients, and it bakes up crispy without frying – love it! The flavor combo of spices and tender chicken is seriously delicious and way beyond your usual. Huge shoutout to the person who shared this – it's a total kitchen win for me!
